# A Claude seat cannot start a second session of itself

## Context

Operator ruling, 2026-10-15: one seat is one session inside its harness. The reason given: a parallel session would get the four Neo MCP servers, read the seat's A2A mailbox and reply as the seat without its context, and the result is chaos.

Claude Desktop now offers its sessions tools that start other sessions, and its system prompt nudges a session proposal on most turns. On 2026-10-14 this happened on `@neo-opus-vega`'s seat: a side session started through `mcp__ccd_session__start_session` ran with every Neo MCP server and wrote Memory Core turns as `@neo-opus-vega` (for example `99564efd`). Two more session proposals followed the same evening. Nothing in the seat's permissions stopped any of it.

## The Problem

Identity belongs to the seat, not the session. A second session shares the seat's GitHub account, A2A identity and Memory Core identity, but none of the first session's context. It can mark the seat's mail read, answer peers, post reviews or claim lanes, all as the seat, and it can contradict or duplicate the first session.

§swarm_topology_anchor already forbids fan-out, and the template denies `Workflow` for that reason (neo#13698). The Desktop's newer spawning tools are not covered, and a memory rule held per seat does not hold against a prompt that nudges on every turn.

## The Architectural Reality

- `.claude/settings.template.json` → `permissions.deny` holds `Workflow` plus the git and merge guards. Each seat's `.claude/settings.json` is generated from the template and gitignored. The Brain materializer copies the template only into an absent `settings.json`, so existing seats adopt a change by explicit copy, as with #19650.
- Tools that start another session from a Claude Desktop seat:
  - `mcp__ccd_session__start_session` and `mcp__ccd_session__hand_off_to_session`, the Desktop session tools;
  - `mcp__scheduled-tasks__create_scheduled_task` and `mcp__scheduled-tasks__run_scheduled_task`, since each run is a new session. No seat has a scheduled task today (`list_scheduled_tasks` on Vega's seat: none).
- Re-invoking the same session (`ScheduleWakeup`, `CronCreate`, `/loop`) creates no second session and stays allowed. The `Agent` tool stays governed by §swarm_topology_anchor (the operator's explicit permission).

## The Fix

Add the four tool names to `permissions.deny` in `.claude/settings.template.json`. Nothing else in the file moves. After the merge, copy the four entries into each Claude seat's generated `.claude/settings.json`: neo-opus-vega, neo-opus-ada, neo-opus-grace, neo-fable and neo-fable-clio.

|---|---|---|---|
| `permissions.deny` in `.claude/settings.template.json` | §swarm_topology_anchor; operator ruling 2026-10-15 | The four spawning tools are refused in every Claude seat. The operator still starts sessions from the app UI, and same-session wakeups are unaffected. | JSON validity and an array diff against `dev`; post-merge, the seats' generated settings carry the entries and a spawn attempt is refused |

Decision Record impact: none. This is aligned with §swarm_topology_anchor and the neo#13698 fan-out deny.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: `permissions.deny` in `.claude/settings.template.json` gains exactly the four tool names; the rest of the file is unchanged.
- [ ] AC-2 (post-merge): all five Claude seats' generated `.claude/settings.json` carry the four entries.
- [ ] AC-3 (post-merge): in a fresh Claude Desktop session on a seat with the entries, `mcp__ccd_session__start_session` is refused or not offered. Probe it with an already-dismissed proposal id, which cannot start anything.

## Out of Scope

The `Agent` tool, same-session wakeups, the operator's own UI, and non-Claude harnesses (Codex, Antigravity), whose spawn surfaces differ.

## Avoided Traps

- A memory-only rule: it is per seat, it decays, and the prompt nudges every turn.
- Denying the whole `mcp__ccd_session` server: that would also block `dismiss_task`, which withdraws a stale proposal.

## Related

#13698 (fan-out deny precedent), #19650 (template rollout semantics).
